scope: Isolated numeric-transport restore race prototype, not an integrated fix
diagnostic: A previously selected numeric candidate is mutated while the next asynchronous lookup runs. Before the prototype, the restored first array contains the changed value rather than the saved value.
prototype: Keep staging bytes for reused candidates until all asynchronous reconstruction completes, then revalidate without yielding and replace changed candidates before assembling the graph.

validation.before: Race regression failed: expected 1, received 999; 16 other transport tests passed.
validation.after: 52 transport, numeric reuse, encoding-client and decoding-client tests passed, including graph alias preservation and unchanged second candidate reuse.
validation.viteBuild: Direct Vite build passed; complete production build and typecheck were not run.
validation.realPly3: Not run: observed free disk was approximately 3.80 GB, below the established 4.00 GB initial admission guard. The guard was not lowered.

limitations: The reproducer uses a low-level callback; a normal GUI or MCP mutation has not been demonstrated.
The prototype keeps staging buffers alive longer, so it may exceed the 4 GiB resource budget on the real workload.
This does not prove safety against mutation after the restored graph is published, nor does it establish GUI or MCP lifecycle acceptance.
